org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils::isAnyOf (full body incl. fault line `if (!pair || j == searchLast) { return true; }`)
rationale: All four premises check out against the patch: indexOfAnyBut's body is only an empty-check plus delegation to firstIndexOutside; the chain firstIndexOutside->memberAt->classifyAt->lookupAt->isAnyOf is as displayed; classifyAt computes pair correctly (index<len-1 and high surrogate); isAnyOf, with pair=true and j<searchLast, never compares searchChars[j+1] to cs.charAt(index+1), so U+20000 at index 0 is rejected and firstIndexOutside returns 0. The agent's narrative therefore places the first wrong value exactly at the gold's fault line. Rank 1 rests solely on premise 1's inference that the 'direct failing API' mishandles pairs, which premise 2 itself refutes. A two-line delegator whose code is correct is not a defensible fault location; the facade was ranked first because the test calls it.
